classification.difficultyReason: The requested similarity proofs guide students to routine angle relationships; finding the lengths then links corresponding-side ratios with Pythagoras and subtraction.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that triangle $ABC$ is similar to triangle $DEC$ and find the value of $e$ and $c$.

spec.description: Opposing triangles share C; A, C, D are collinear and B, C, E are collinear. Matching arrows show AB parallel to DE. Ordinary source-blue geometry is reconstructed in house black.
spec.mathematics: AB=6 cm, BC=4 cm, AC=5 cm, CE=6 cm, CD=e cm, DE=c cm; AB parallel to DE.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied labels remain visible; no calculated lengths appear.

answer.short:
$\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEC$ (AAA); $e=7\frac12$ and $c=9$.

Use alternate and vertically opposite angles, then the matching-side ratio $\frac{6}{4}$.
answer.worked:
$\angle BAC=\angle CDE$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel DE$).

$\angle BCA=\angle ECD$ (vertically opposite angles).

Therefore $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DEC$ (AAA).

Matching sides are proportional:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{CD}{AC}&=\frac{CE}{BC}\\\frac{e}{5}&=\frac{6}{4}\\e&=5\times\frac{6}{4}\\e&=\frac{15}{2}=7\frac12.\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\frac{DE}{AB}&=\frac{CE}{BC}\\\frac{c}{6}&=\frac{6}{4}\\c&=6\times\frac{6}{4}\\c&=9.\end{align*}$$
Thus $CD=7\frac12\text{ cm}$ and $DE=9\text{ cm}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Prove that triangle $JNK$ is similar to triangle $JML$ and find the values of $x$ and $y$.

spec.description: Nested right triangles share J and the ray JM. The external double-ended dimension arrow spans JN only. Ordinary geometry is black.
spec.mathematics: J,K,L collinear; J,N,M collinear; KN perpendicular to JL and LM perpendicular to JL; JN=5 cm, KN=3 cm, LM=5 cm, JK=x cm, KL=y cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied dimensions and unknowns only; calculated values are absent.

answer.short:
$\triangle JNK\sim\triangle JML$ (AAA); $x=4$ and $y=2\frac23$.

Use the common angle and right angles, Pythagoras in $JNK$, then proportional sides.
answer.worked:
$\angle NJK=\angle MJL$ (common angle at $J$).

$\angle NKJ=\angle MLJ=90^\circ$ (given).

Therefore $\triangle JNK\sim\triangle JML$ (AAA).

By Pythagoras in $\triangle JNK$:
$$\begin{align*}JK^2&=JN^2-KN^2\\JK^2&=5^2-3^2\\JK^2&=16\\JK&=4\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
Hence $x=4$.

Matching sides are proportional:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{JL}{JK}&=\frac{LM}{NK}\\\frac{JL}{4}&=\frac{5}{3}\\JL&=\frac{20}{3}\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}KL&=JL-JK\\KL&=\frac{20}{3}-4\\KL&=\frac{8}{3}\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
Thus $y=\frac83=2\frac23$.
